newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian central bank mulls future sale of gold.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian central bank mulls future sale of gold.

text.p: The Bank of Lithuania said on Thursday it was considering following the lead of other central banks by selling off some of its gold reserves in the future.
"So far we don't plan to make any sales but we have some ideas about that for the future," the central bank governor, Reinoldijus Sharkinas, told Reuters.

"We are considering the possibility in order to change the share of gold in our foreign reserves," Sharkinas added. "Today, gold makes more than six percent of foreign reserves, and in the future we could sell part of it."
"The earnings on invested gold are lower than those that we could receive investing in foreign exchange," Sharkinas said.
He added that Lithuania would not sell any of its gold reserves this year.
The Bank of Lithuania's official reserves as of the end of June were $939.6 million, of which $62.1 million was gold.
